name: serde_json
listed_description: Rust JSON crate used with serde derive to read a JSON file into typed structures and write structures back out as JSON.
book_benchmark: None. Book shows only convenience of from_str and to_string with derived traits; no timings. The crate README (not the book) claims competitiveness with the fastest C and C++ JSON libraries.
found_in: book: Rust for C++ Developers (2026), ch. 6, Simple serialization and deserialization, Reading a JSON file using serde

name: serde
listed_description: Generic serialization and deserialization framework for Rust; derive macros generate typed (de)serializers with attributes for renames, defaults and unknown fields.
found_in: book: Rust for C++ Developers (2026), ch. 6, Simple serialization and deserialization, Customizing serialization behavior

name: byteorder
listed_description: Crate adding extension traits to Read and Write for reading and writing integers and floats with explicit big-endian or little-endian byte order.
guessed_baseline: hand-written shifts, htonl and ntohl style byte swaps
found_in: book: Rust for C++ Developers (2026), ch. 6, Reading and Writing Files, Extending the I/O APIs

name: sha256 (Rust crate)
listed_description: Rust crate used in the book's opening example to hash a file contents with a few lines of code after cargo add sha256.
book_benchmark: None. Book uses it to show dependency ease against hunting for a licensed C++ SHA-256 library; no timings.
found_in: book: Rust for C++ Developers (2026), ch. 1, Why Choose Rust?, High level, low level
